title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 3
paragraphs: While Darius had not yet made his decision, it happened that Demaratus son of Ariston had come up to Susa at this very time, having been deprived of his kingship at Sparta and having imposed on himself an exile from Lacedaemon. When he heard about the quarrel between Darius's sons, this man — so the story goes — advised Xerxes to add to his usual arguments the following point: that he had been born to Darius after Darius was already reigning as king and held the supreme power over the Persians, while Artobazanes had been born while Darius was still a private man; it was not fitting, therefore, or just, that another should take precedence over him, for even at Sparta, Demaratus said, the custom was this: if some sons had been born first, before their father began to reign, and another came later, born while he was reigning, the succession belonged to the son born later. Xerxes used this argument of Demaratus; and Darius, seeing the justice of it, designated him king. In my own opinion, though, Xerxes would have become king even without this suggestion, since Atossa was all-powerful.
